answer: A burn registry stops sybil attacks by requiring proof of destruction. First, an agent selects $250 worth of POA tokens. Second, they send these to a provably unspendable address. Third, the registry issues a unique identity tied to this burn hash. Finally, peers verify this "skin in the game" before attesting. This concrete $250 cost causes an attacker's resource pool to reach its nadir quickly. Even a comet-fast botnet cannot afford mass entry. This ensures only committed agents taste the nectar of protocol yields. It is like a club where entry requires burning a high-value bill at the door.
